payload.raid_opened:
R1 THE SECRET LEAVES THE MACHINE (risk, owner: owner, HIGH). The brief carries the gate's actual content - what is being decided, on what evidence - to a third-party host. Mitigation by design: the page is encrypted and the key rides the URL fragment, which browsers never send to the server, so the host holds ciphertext only. Residual accepted: whoever holds the link holds the content, which is the same possession model the owner already ruled for the topic (v1's adr-answer-authenticity). TRIGGER: any change that would put plaintext in KV, or any brief that would carry a credential rather than a decision.

R2 THE TOKEN (risk, owner: agent). Publishing needs the cloudflare_kv token. It must never be logged, never land in a brief, never reach the ledger, and never be echoed in a run record - the same discipline i8 kept for the ntfy token. TRIGGER: the build's first publish; the check is that no logged object contains it.

R3 EVENTUAL CONSISTENCY (risk, owner: agent). KV is ~60s eventually consistent, so a notification sent immediately can point at a page that is not yet servable - the design records this as the implementation lesson from the 2026-07-21 dry run. Mitigation: read-after-write, verify the serve URL responds, and only then notify. TRIGGER: the M6 spike, which must reproduce and defeat it rather than assume.

R4 THE UNVERIFIED LEG SHIPS AGAIN (risk, owner: agent, HIGH). This iteration exists because a leg the design flagged as unverified shipped untested, and its replacement has the same hazard - a publish that returns 200 while the phone renders nothing tappable. Mitigation: M6 is not a code spike but a LIVE one, ending in a real tap on a real phone; the owner's bless of this iteration's own release gate IS the acceptance. TRIGGER: any claim of 'the transport works' that is not backed by a tap.

R5 THE HOST GOES AWAY (assumption, owner: owner). The whole tier-1 rung rests on a free Cloudflare account, one worker and one KV namespace, all set up manually in 2026-07-21 and unowned by any code. If it lapses or the token is rotated, the rich brief silently degrades. Mitigation, and it is the ladder's whole point: the card with its actions still works without a host, so the failure is a downgrade rather than an outage - provided it is REPORTED. TRIGGER: a publish failing for auth or DNS reasons.

R6 SILENT DEGRADATION (issue, owner: agent). Today nothing reports whether a publish succeeded, so any of R3-R5 would look identical to a working lane. This is pulled in as a requirement rather than left as a risk, because it is what made the current defect invisible for a whole day. TRIGGER: closed by the build; the check is that a failed publish is visible without reading the code.
